title: Choose the visual world (safer re-roll)
question: Three calmer directions, plus the standing exit. Keep one, ask for more or less of it, or re-roll.
channel: Crush question form with pictures (owner's standing preference: look choices in the form, no pop-up pages)
ownerWords: Round 1 answers: none of the three, show three different ones; less of it (calmer, closer to a normal app); paid GPT image. Competitor bar: Zed, plus "A little more dazzle than these apps have."
kept: The general design (three columns: chat list with branch tree, conversation, visuals panel with the limits row) stays; the world changes.

bar.note: As tidy as Zed (aligned grid, even spacing, a real type scale), with a little more dazzle than Zed has.

options.label: Standards Manual
options.thesis: Crush run like a standards manual: a strict grid, Helvetica, black and white, and one red that only ever marks where you are.
options.viewport: Standard three columns. A red logotype at top left; red marks the selected chat, its branch line, the branch words and the current flow step; the three usage numbers set large in bold Helvetica.
options.signature: A single red rule system that shows where you are at every level.
options.risk: Red usually means error, so real warnings must keep amber; Helvetica on black can feel cold.

options.label: Drawing Set
options.lineage: engineering drawing sets: ISO title blocks, revision tables, blueprint linework
options.thesis: Every chat is a sheet and every branch a revision with its letter.
options.viewport: Standard three columns in ink blue, messages unboxed on the panel. Revision triangles with letters mark each branch in the chat list and on the branch words.
options.redraw: First draw added a literal drawing-sheet title block (invented date, NOT TO SCALE) and boxed every message, caused by the prompt's 'ruled title block' line; prompt corrected and redrawn once.
options.risk: A lot of blue can feel cold or corporate; the triangles must stay small or they read as warning signs.

options.label: Preprint
options.lineage: LaTeX article class, Computer Modern, Tufte-style sidenotes
options.thesis: Crush set like a preprint: calm paper, serif text, and every branch a numbered sidenote.
materials: yellow highlighter mark on branch words
options.viewport: Standard three columns on paper white. The chat list numbers branches 1.1 and 1.2; the branch words carry a highlighter mark and a superscript pointing to a sidenote in the chat's margin.
options.signature: Branches as numbered sidenotes from highlighted words.
options.risk: Light theme; serif text can feel slow or like homework, and code reads worse in a serif world.

canonCard.label: Keep the current look
canonCard.thesis: The category standard, played straight: charcoal and amber, as in style-2, held to Zed's finish.
canonCard.risk: What most AI chat apps look like.
